extracted.intended_audience: prospective attendees / writers interested in applying to or learning about the Community of Writers conference
extracted.subtask_description: Information and informal criteria for applying to and evaluating the Community of Writers summer conference (admission procedure, workshop formats, faculty, financial aid, and publication outcomes). Useful for writers deciding whether to apply or for comparing writers' conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Community has a formal and competitive admissions procedure. Applicants are asked to submit an application fee and a writing sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page states an application fee and a writing sample are required. It notes the procedure is 'formal and competitive' and that independent sourcing is needed for some details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rate (selectivity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This figure gives an empirical measure of selectivity; the article presents it as an average. The page flags some statements as needing independent sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid / scholarships availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Roughly 50% of those who attend are granted some form of financial aid. Scholarships and financial aid is provided through the donations for alumni, staff and friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates substantial availability of aid; no detailed eligibility criteria given on the page. Some statements marked 'independent source needed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop genres offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops are held in fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and screenwriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists the four primary workshop tracks and names directors for each (e.g., fiction directors Lisa D. Alvarez and Louis B. Jones; nonfiction director Michael Carlisle; poetry director Robert Hass; screenwriting director Diana Fuller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop size and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference generally offers 8 fiction workshops of 12 participants each and two narrative nonfiction/memoir workshops of 12 each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates small, workshop-sized cohorts (12 participants) and the overall number of workshop sections; the line is followed by a '[citation needed]' tag on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program components (panels, talks, readings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels, talks, staff readings and workshops take place in off-season ski lodge facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the program format beyond workshops — panels, talks, staff readings — and the conference setting, which informs participant experience and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty quality / notable teaching staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Noted authors and recent teaching staff are listed (many well-known poets, fiction and nonfiction writers, and screenwriters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists numerous prominent writers associated as faculty (e.g., Robert Hass, Galway Kinnell, Anne Lamott, Alice Sebold, Yiyun Li, Amy Tan, Ada Limón, etc.), which serves as an implicit quality metric for the conference; many entries are marked 'independent source needed' in places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialty workshops / legacy programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference has run specialty offerings such as the 'Finding the Story Workshop' taught by Gill Dennis and long-running poetry program leadership (e.g., Galway Kinnell reinvented and directed the Poetry Program for 17 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of named, longstanding special programs indicates curricular depth and continuity; historical notes illustrate program evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and alumni outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poetry Program publishes an annual anthology of poems first written at the workshop. A book, Writers Workshop in a Book: The S.V. Community of Writers on the Art of Fiction, was published in 2007.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists program outputs and publications that demonstrate opportunities for work produced at the conference to be published or otherwise disseminated; also includes an alumni reading series that features recently published attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni prominence as a quality indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Many notable writers and poets are listed as alumni (e.g., Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie, Michael Chabon, Jennifer Egan, Anne Rice, Lev Grossman, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of high-profile alumni is presented implicitly as evidence of the conference's stature and the potential professional benefit for attendees; the page includes extensive alumni lists.
